utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I would first kindly ask the usher to distribute the document which I just gave when we stopped yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Kovacic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While we're having the document distributed, perhaps just one question that I omitted during the first part. Mr. Sajevic, you work in the National Security Service of the BiH Federation today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is the most important organ in the BiH Federation that is involved in matters related to the security of the country; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether it's the most important, because there are security organs in the armed forces as well, but it is one of the most important, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. The document has been distributed, so let us dwell on it for a moment, very briefly. Yesterday we mentioned that after the army took away the weapons of the Territorial Defence, a bit later weapons were taken from companies as well. The first document we have here is a certificate of the handover of ammunition and weapons. Can you confirm to the Court that this first document clearly shows that the weapons handed over, according to this list -- there is a description of the weapons here, and these are the weapons that were in the SPS factory. It was handed over to the municipal headquarters of the TO, that is, the end of 1990, that is, the 7th of November, 1990. At that time you worked at the Territorial Defence and you are aware of these events, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. At that time I did work in the Territorial Defence. I'm aware of this event and I can confirm that what you said is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The second document that we have is a letter of the Council for National Defence of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me follow this first document. Is this a document -- it may be that the second one explains it, but I'm looking at the first one -- a document showing the transfer of arms from the SPS, TO, carried out by Mario Cerkez? And then there's a list of the items handed over, but where will I find where they're handed over to?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the usher please put the document back on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document shows that it was handed over by the company to the Territorial Defence, and we're going to ask the witness what the future fate of this was. We just see the first stage of the operation here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us do this in an orderly fashion. This document, two pages, is that right, three pages in the English?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: -- of the 9th of November, should have first of all an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Kovacic. If you could get the witness briefly to explain it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, you have heard the Honourable Judge. Could you please explain what this first document shows.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is the way it was. When the Galib action began, that is to say, when weapons were first taken from the Territorial Defence, first the weapons were taken away and put into the warehouses of the Territorial Defence headquarters that had warehouses of their own. However, it was probably more difficult for them to look for weapons, or rather to seek weapons from a work organisation, such as the SPS was. That was the factory that bought these weapons with their own money, and they had adequate storage facilities for the mentioned weapons. In addition to that, they had guards of their own, watchmen, around the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Major Sajevic, I asked what the document said. Now, could you please explain the document. Don't tell us about the background or anything else; just explain what the document says, in a few words.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document shows that Mr. Mario Cerkez, who was in charge of these resources, handed over these resources to the municipal headquarters of the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just an additional question related to this document. The document shows -- is this correct, that this was done with the participation of a certain commission? Its members are mentioned here. I'm talking about page 3 of the document, or rather the last page of this document, and the head of the service of the SPS that was involved in this particular activity, Dusan Lukovic, also signed this, and on the other side there's a signature of the Territorial Defence Commander. That is where you were; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The next document I would like to ask for a number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next document in this set of documents bears the same date, and it is a document of the Council for National Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This actually shows that the transfer that we saw in the first document is actually being requested; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now we'd like to look at the next document, please, and I'd kindly ask for a number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There is a list here, a chart, that actually corroborates what the first document says, and that is exactly what was handed over.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly. And can I just add something to this?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also there are the numbers of the orders that we got from the Municipal Staff of National Defence and also from The National Defence Council of the municipality of Vitez, so all those documents are there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of which all of this was carried out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the last document. I would like to ask you for a number again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The last document is a copy of a newspaper article from those days. It is dated the 8th of April, 1991. As a citizen in that area at the time, do you know which newspaper this is?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I imagine this was a Sarajevo evening newspaper.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the excerpt here says that in Vitez, specifically, of course, the citizens reacted to all of this, because the factory bought weapons with money of their own and then somebody took it away from them. And the workers who voted within the self-management system of the enterprise, who allocated money for the purchase of weapons, were now actually putting the question where the weapons are. Do you agree with this assessment?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct on the basis of everything that we have been discussing so far that weapons were taken away from socially-owned enterprises at the time, that is to say, in the months of October and November in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened then?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Before you go on, we ought to have a number for the newspaper article.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the Territorial Defence do with the weapons at the time, the Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence in Vitez, actually?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Municipal Staff of the Territorial Defence in Vitez transported these weapons and other equipment to the warehouses of the JNA where the rest of the weapons were too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the basis of everything that we have said until now about these weapons, is it clear that the Yugoslav Peoples' Army which, at that time, was practically under the control of one republic only, the Republic of Serbia, in this way basically disarmed the republics? First they took the Territorial Defence weapons of the municipal organisations, and then they even took the weapons that were the property of enterprises and that were purchased by these same enterprises; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my profound conviction.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can proceed now. Witness Sajevic, from the end of 1991, certain things started happening and they were reflected in all walks of life including in the Territorial Defence where you worked. Is it correct that this was the first time that divisions arose and different views were expressed, all of this on the basis of ethnic differences? Can you explain the process to us?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally noticed that there were certain divisions. At first, these were only differences in views, different approaches of individuals to this problem. Especially after the attack on the village of Ravno where Croats were the victims, the Bosniak members of the Territorial Defence staff, probably in pursuit of their official policy, simply believed that this was none of their business. However, the Croats, in my opinion, made the right assessment as to what lay in store for us, and things could not have been the same when we realised what was going on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, you, the Croats in Bosnia, saw what was happening in Croatia as well; is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Generally speaking, on the basis of what you've said, did it become clear that the Bosniak side, during everything that was going on in 1990 and 1991, simply kept their distance from the entire problem not expecting all these terrible things to happen to them as well? Could that be said?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: However you Croats in Bosnia, can we say that you were more sensitive to this precisely because the Croat people of Croatia were attacked at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in part because of that, but also in part because we saw what the situation was like and how it was developing from Slovenia to Croatia, and we came to the conclusion that something similar awaited us as well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Little by little this process took its course. Is it correct that at that time, already in 1992, for example, in the spring of 1992, you felt quite unwanted in the Territorial Defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, you said beginning of 1992?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, the beginning of 1992, the spring of 1992, you tell us exactly. When did you first realise that you were not really wanted there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, certain differentiations started already the beginning of 1992, when certain planned activities of the TO started taking place. I'm referring to regular administrative activities. Also, some training was conducted for the Command Staff itself and, in a way, there was a certain division into groups. The members of the Bosniak people were trying to impose their own method of work, if I can put it that way. And these differentiations became more pronounced from day-to-day until they finally culminated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the volume of your work actually decreased because you were not allowed to carry out your duties, it was other people who were now carrying out your duties; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that SDA meetings, that is to say party meetings took place in Territorial Defence offices?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that various documents were being concealed from the Croat members of the Territorial Defence staff, that is to say, the Bosniaks were doing that so that you the Croat members could not see certain documents and information?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And could you just tell me one more thing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't lead.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't lead from now on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me now, finally, how you got out of the Territorial Defence staff, how all of this ended?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was, in fact, expelled from the Territorial Defence staff in the following way: One morning I came to work as usual. At that time, the Territorial Defence staff was already outside its peacetime premises, that is to say, in a house that is about, I don't know, 400, 500 metres away from our former premises. I entered the main room, we called it the operations room. Then my former colleague walked up to me, a man who had worked with me before, Muhamed Patkovic, and he started with accusations, saying that I was a traitor or something to that effect. He called a guard who was in front of the building at the entrance, that is, and he said, "Sajevic should be disarmed and detained." The guard said the following to him: "Muhamed, you should be disarmed first and then him." Why he said that, I really don't know. At any rate, I left the premises of the then headquarters and I never returned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, please, at that moment, was there any reason, any reason whatsoever, for the Territorial Defence as an institution to take any kind of legal action against you as employees of the Territorial Defence, any kind of action to have you dismissed, to take any kind of action? Did you do something in order to deserve that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that I did not do anything to justify such proceedings. Even more so because in the same room, there were four or five other members of the staff as well who were also surprised, at least apparently, by what he did and said, "Muhamed, what's the matter with you? What are you doing?" But I just turned around and I walked out and I had no further contact with them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, amongst those present, there were both Croats and Muslims at the time still?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think at that time there was only one Croat colleague still there, Goran something or other. I don't remember his last name. And of the Muslims, that is Bosniaks, Sulejman Kalco was present, Zenada Cousevic. I know about the two of them. I can't remember who the others were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, of course. And do you remember if, at that time, the Territorial Defence had already been left by Zeljko Vrebac a colleague of yours?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Zeljko Vrebac was still there at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So he left after you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, a few days after me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about Mrs. Anna Granic, when did she leave, before or after you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before me. I don't even think she had been invited as a member of the TO staff to that forward command post in that house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean she's already dropped out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about Dravko Livancic, when did he leave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dravko Livancic left before me but he but he did not side with the Croat people, to put it that way, but he went to Zenica -- but he was in the barracks in Zenica with the JNA. And later on, allegedly, he went to Zepce and --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, right. But is it correct that this situation was forced on him that he simply could not but leave?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Muhamed Patkovic whom you mentioned in the later days of the war, what kind of a man did he turn out to be?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him very seldom, perhaps on a couple of occasions only, and after that, I stopped seeing them altogether. But I heard from his colleagues and after the war when we talked, that he had joined that -- what should I call it, I don't really know -- this Mujahedin movement of those happily warriors, or something, something in that vein. But I don't know. I did not see him. I did not talk to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But we can agree, whatever the case, that he was one of the more extreme members of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am profoundly convicted about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in 1993, he was Commander, precisely in that area, in the Vitez pocket, one of the Commanders, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Yes. Surely he was a Commander. I don't know at what level, but undoubtedly he was one of the Commanders in those areas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that his name came up in some reports in 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember just now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. The organisation of the HVO staff also roughly began at the same time with these happenings in the Territorial Defence, so could we perhaps date it to May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we could say that that was roughly the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time did the Territorial Defence form some units, armed units, and then send them to some front lines against the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, the Territorial Defence did form some units and sent them to fight the Serbs, I think somewhere in the direction of Visoko, which is nowhere near the boundaries of our municipality, so that practically it did not exercise its proper function in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In April 1992, the state of war was officially proclaimed by the President or the Presidency of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that correct? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time the Territorial Defence was moved to the "Yellow House" at Podgradina?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could we agree, Mr. Sajevic, that as of May 1992 not one Croat remained in the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think, yes, we could agree about that. Without going into the exact date, I can't remember, but I think that as of May there was nobody left.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. At the Municipal Staff that we've already mentioned, which began to come into existence at the time, what was its task?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Municipal Staff of the Croat Defence Council was tasked to try to organise in whatever way possible the Croat people in Vitez. And I believe the same held true of other municipalities, to organise for the struggle against the JNA and the Serb aggressor, because at that time there had already been the shelling of Vitez and Busovaca. Serb aircraft, I mean, combat aircraft, could still fly over and shell those areas. And at the same time, in the areas of Turbe and Vlasic, the Serb forces were amassing, so it was logical to assume that they were getting ready to come down into the Lasva Valley and take certain areas, which meant that we had to work towards the organisation of our defence.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And within the framework of all this, this desire to organise one's own defence, was it by that time clear that nobody else would organise this defence for the Croats, because the Territorial Defence was not aware or was not perceiving this danger of war in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time we were clear that the Territorial Defence was not perceiving this problem in the same light; however, we were -- there was readiness on our part and there were attempts to achieve an understanding with the Bosniak side about the establishment of joint formations which would then be engaged in the defence of Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. But let us not move to the joint formation until we've finished with this. You told us that the municipal HVO defence staffs were to organise the people, to organise the defence. Is it correct that from this organisational point of view, from the point of view of organisation, these staffs had to organise the mobilisation or the affairs related to mobilisation, things that were before that discharged by the municipal boards for national defence, what we talked about, that is, to prepare the lists of conscripts, their addresses, and so on and so forth; all that goes with the mobilisation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, quite correct. One of the principal, one of the primary tasks of the municipal staffs was at least to have an overview of able-bodied men in the municipal territories and to try to organise it somehow. Because at the time we were compiling those lists and everything else, we were quite clear that at that time we could not count with the members of Bosniak ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the municipal staffs also assumed that other function, which was previously divided --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Stop leading.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Sorry. I didn't have my microphone on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My idea was only to be faster, but certainly there is no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Bring the witness to the point. Ask him briefly to describe what happened. But evidence which is given by counsel does not have any value. Ask him what the purpose -- what did the municipal staffs do? What was their purpose? Can you deal with that, Major Sajevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, which was the other function of the staff?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other function of the staff was at first to bring together the volunteers in the municipality of Vitez and to organise them in groups -- one cannot speak about formations or anything -- and then to try to conduct certain minor operations with those volunteers against the Serb aggressor on Vlasic, at Turbe and so on. And those Vitez volunteers launched those operations, but when they would come back they would simply go home, naturally, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And who was the Chief of the Staff since its -- as of its foundation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Marijan Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the order of magnitude, what was it? How many people got together in the staff, as a skeleton?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this first skeleton, I think we were some six or seven of us, approximately.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was the second accused, Mario Cerkez, also part of the group?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mario Cerkez was in that group, as a kind of -- how shall I call it? -- deputy to Marijan Skopljak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was there any difference in the jobs that Marijan and Cerkez [as interpreted] discharged during the existence of the Municipal Staff between April and December?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean Marijan Skopljak?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Marijan Skopljak was responsible for the policies of that institution. And Mr. Mario Cerkez's responsibility mostly came down to logistics, when it came to the equipment of the groups which went out to conduct certain operations, and he at times headed those groups. I think that that was what I might call his primary task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But is it true that his role was that he was slowly, to put it that way, was climbing up the hierarchical ladder in that system?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We could say that he was advancing, because he was involved in that from the beginning, so naturally he was advancing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, tell us, please: That organisation, from when it took shape until December 1992, did it have any rigid organisation, that is, job description, communication between people, and so on?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, come. No. There was no rigid organisation, nor had it been laid down by any document. There were no rules on labour relations as before, nor did we who worked there have any decisions appointing us to individual jobs. I should say it was all on a voluntary basis, all self-organised, and so on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You no doubt know that Mr. Cerkez directly participated in several combat operations in the activities of the staff against the Serbs, that is, that he personally took part in some operations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you give us some examples? I know it's difficult to remember all of those stories today.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for instance, on Turbe up there, then on Vlasic. I can't forget -- oh, yes, Galica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Cerkez ever participate in Jajce fighting?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that he did it directly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did he perhaps organise departures for Jajce?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did do that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that all those operations were only and exclusively against the then-aggressor, which was the JNA, or rather the army of Bosnian Serbs?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No doubt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time -- we're talking about 1992 -- were there any plans or ideas that a conflict with Bosnian Muslims might happen?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at the time when the front line was established on Vlasic against the Serbs, then both sides -- that is, the BH army, which had been established in the meantime, and the HVO -- held certain segments of that front facing the Serbs; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly regarding the positions of the BH army, because I was not up there directly, but I know that our guys went up there. And the positions of the Armija and in what numbers were present there, I wouldn't know. But I think that as far as the BH army was concerned, at that time I do not think they were up there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Later on, when it became clear that both armies were up there, was there any coordination there between them?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I cannot say with certainty. There should have been. It was called for to know who was on the left and who was on the right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And Mr. Sajevic, after all, could you tell us: When did the staff stop its activity? The municipal HVO staff in Vitez, when did it stop functioning?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the municipal HVO staff in Vitez terminated its work sometime in the autumn of 1992, when the Defence Office in Vitez was set up, and Marijan Skopljak was appointed the Chief of the Defence Office. And it then took over the organisation and all other work related to this aspect of work. And the rest -- and some other people left and the rest of the staff remained there hanging in the air, so to speak, undefined. Those were the early days of the formation of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, at that moment, when the office -- when the Defence Office in the municipality was formed and when Marijan Skopljak and some men took over that office and began to discharge those activities, you who remained in that staff, who didn't really know what to do. You had already been told by the HVO government that the intention was to set up the brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that, as a matter of fact, you were waiting from one day to the other for the brigade to be formed?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, quite true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you were waiting, could you tell us if certain shifts went to Vlasic during that period of time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The shifts being sent -- at that time shifts to Jajce were already been sent.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that at that time it was a matter of routine?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you could say that it was a routine job, even though there were problems here and there regarding the formation of the shifts, because we practically had no instruments of coercion or discipline to simply make a military conscript to go. It was all practically on the voluntary basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that when a military conscript would get summons, and if he felt morally bound to respond, then he would respond; but if he did not, then nobody could take him away by force?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, nobody could take him away by force. He could devise a thousand reasons not to go.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And just a few technical details concerning the staff. Where was the first headquarters of the Municipal Staff when it was established?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the first headquarters were practically housed at Marijan Skopljak's. Those were the early days, when the whole staff was being set up. And then in the Vitez Hotel was the headquarters of the Municipal Staff throughout.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And after the hotel?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the hotel, the Defence Office of Vitez was established, and after the hotel, the brigade -- or rather we found -- we established -- we, this backbone of a kind, who were bringing together these volunteers for the shifts, and until the establishment of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, when we moved to Novi Travnik. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that I wouldn't know the date exactly, but the military district of Vitez then moved into those offices in Hotel Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And by "military district," you mean the Operative Zone commanded by Tihomir Blaskic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Perhaps we should explain to the Court, because in some documents later there is different terminology. There's military district, Operative Zone. Is it one and the same thing? And what was the official name?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At first, in the beginning of 1992, the official name was the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia. I think that at that time, I don't know, I'm not too sure whether Tihomir Blaskic headed the Operative Zone from the outset. I think it was Filip Filipovic at first, and then it changed its name into the military district of Vitez headed by Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At any rate, both terms, the Operative Zone and the military district mean the same thing, that is the Regional Command of Central Bosnia; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that during a brief period, a rather short period after your headquarters was in the hotel, it was then moved to the cinema already after Blaskic arrived in Vitez; do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that at that time, when we went from the hotel to Novi Travnik to the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade, at that time, the Command came to Vitez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned this a while ago but perhaps we should clarify it. In the spring of 1992, and all the way up to the early summer, there were some activities that you mentioned in an effort to conduct joint actions, joint in the sense of BH army and the HVO, the HVO headquarters in Vitez and the other side you did not -- did you cooperate well with them? You tried to organise a joint defence against the Serbs, against the JNA. What was all this about?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, can you please try and ask short questions; short, focussed and neutral questions. Simply ask: Was there any cooperation in the summer of 1992 between the TO and the HVO? We'll get on more quickly. The matter will be dealt with neutrally rather than you making a speech.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise my intention was to lead the story to make it shorter, but I will certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question of cooperation at that time, the spring and early summer of 1992, the attempts and the plans that were made, were there any plans?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were plans. Together with the Bosniak side, certain units were supposed to be set up in order to act in defence against the Serb aggressor. One form of cooperation was the exchange, so to speak, of certain types of weapons. That is to say, that if we had something that they needed, I mean if we had a surplus then we would exchange that. However, on several occasions, meetings were scheduled with the representatives of the Territorial Defence and the army. Well, the TO actually, I think we can call it that now. There were supposed to be concrete resolutions in terms of organising joint efforts. I took part in such meetings myself. In a way, I was delegated by the Croat side. I was supposed to conduct these talks. Franjo Nakic was with me. However, at a few of these meetings, we achieved no results. The last meeting that I recall was at the TO premises. Franjo Nakic and I came to this meeting and after 15 minutes, when this meeting had progressed for 15 minutes already, after the official part, we were told that their side cannot adopt any conclusions or proposals until the SDA party meeting that was taking place then was over. We did not want to wait for the end of that meeting because that was a political party. We thought that we could resolve some of these problems at that level so we left. Those were these attempts to set up joint units.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even a name was envisaged for this joint unit, wasn't there? What was it supposed to be called?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were proposals to call it the Croat Muslim Defence Council. Also, we gave consideration to the establishment of a brigade on the territory of the municipality of Vitez, they should be called the 1st Vitez Brigade. This way, that way. There were different proposals, different ideas.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, this was obviously a process -- or no, rather, was this a process? Was this a process? Did this go on for a while?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During one part of this process, did it seem that things would work out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, to me personally, it seemed that it would work out. We even went so far as to draw up a list of the command of this unit that was supposed to be set up. Some kind of a command of this Croatian Muslim Defence Council which never came into being, but let's call it that way. We wanted to have these different assignments given within the command. Of course, this was never signed and it never went further.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can you tell us definitely, in conclusion, when was this idea finally buried? When did you realise that obviously this could not work out?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we realised that, I think, in the end of August 1992 that nothing would come out of this idea in spite of all the attempts that were made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, in your opinion, in your assessment, you were involved. Was the failure of this idea the result of the attitude of the soldiers in these negotiations or the politicians in these negotiations?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would say it was the politicians and their attitude in these negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you referring to the political parties when you say that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the establishment of the office and of the brigade at that time. Could you please tell us when the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade was established sometime around the beginning of December of 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was its first Commander?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its first Commander was Borivoje Malbasic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where was the first headquarters of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its first headquarters was in the Novi Travnik Hotel.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They started from scratch in the establishment of this brigade. There weren't any units that really preceded it and that then came to constitute this brigade.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, there weren't any official units whose successor it would be, so to speak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was the post held by Mario Cerkez?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Mario Cerkez held the post of Commander of the brigade or rather the Chief of Staff of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your formations at that time, the Chief of Staff was automatically the Deputy Commander; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did Malbasic leave the post of the Commander of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this was in the month of January, 1993. I'm not sure. Or later, later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could it have been in February 1993?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it could have. Yes, it could have been in February. I don't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've had evidence about this. If the witness doesn't remember, don't pursue him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, there's no doubt about this, Cerkez took over the command of this brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. At first he was Acting Commander and then he was Commander.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. There were a few of you from Vitez who were members of the Command; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you remember some names that come to mind?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In addition to Mr. Mario Cerkez and myself, there's the Stipo Ceko, Tomislav Krizanac, there was -- just a moment, please -- Ivo Sucic. I'm trying to remember now according to the different areas where people worked.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. At any rate, there were several of you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this was the only mixed brigade that covered the territory of two municipalities in Central Bosnia at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All other brigades, all other HVO brigades established in December 1992 were strictly on the basis of one municipality, one brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Cerkez had two primary duties in this command from its very inception even when Malbasic was there. Can you tell us what his primary duties were in the briefest possible terms, two or three words only?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: His primary duty, his basic duty was to coordinate, in a way, work with the municipal structures of the municipalities of Vitez and Novi Travnik in terms of logistic support, in terms of the materiel equipment of the brigade. From time to time there was some misunderstandings in this respect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his other task?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To organise the work of the Municipal Staff itself at the command post.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the only task of the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade at the time within its zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's only task was to fight against the Serb aggressor. Its zone of responsibility was where people went from Novi Travnik and Vitez, from Slatka Vode all the way Kamenjas. I can show it on the map, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This sector where the Stjepan Tomasevic Brigade covered this -- I mean it involved men from Vitez and Novi Travnik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were two battalions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These battalions were based on the locations of the municipalities concerned. One was primarily based in Novi Travnik and the other one was primarily based in Vitez; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Mr. Sajevic, you came to this command and you were there at the same time when Cerkez was there, that is to say, December 1992, March 1993. Can you say whether there were any conflicts at that time between the BH army and the HVO in Novi Travnik while you were there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would not say that there were conflicts between the HVO and the BH army. There were some minor incidents. I don't know. Things just happened in the field, probably initiated by individuals. There were no organised conflicts, no way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that there could have been any incident in which the HVO, as a unit, could have taken part in any incident or conflict of smaller proportions or larger proportions at someone's orders?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure of that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sure of that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think we can now move on to the Viteska Brigade. Tell me, please --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, there were many evidences on that matter. Probably my idea is just to show all the documents related to the foundation of the brigade. That is all mentioned more precisely or less precisely until now, and I think it is appropriate time to put all four or five relevant documents in one binder, I should say, and present them together as really detailed picture on how that started.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] While the document is being distributed, we can already move on to that subject. At whose initiative was the Vitez Brigade formed in the municipality, that is, to forego the principle of two municipalities, one brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the initiative came from the HVO government in the municipality of Vitez because to all intents and purposes, this was the only one without it's own formation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And just to tie it up with our first part, this is the logic, the concept of the Territorial Defence which existed in Yugoslavia before the war?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please now look at this first document, document dated 1st of March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the number, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, I hope you had time to look at the document, and will you please tell us, in a few words, what is it that transpires from this document? Who writes to whom, and what is the request about?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document shows that the defence office in Vitez requests from the Command of the Operative Zone of Central Bosnia for some changes in the organisation and mobilisation. They are requesting that the establishment of the brigade of the municipality of Vitez be immediately embarked upon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that would be the initiative that you mentioned. It is the Defence Office which initiates the formation or rather submits such a proposal to the Operative Zone; do we agree about that?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know at the time that there was such an -- that such an initiative had taken place?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did know it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, the next document, and the number, please, the document of the 12 of March 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D81/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you please have a look at the document. Do you agree -- or, no, would you comment on this document? What does it mean? What transpires from it? What is it Cerkez's tasked with?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document is -- well, say, has the weight of an order, that is, the Commander of the Operative Zone or rather the military district, excuse me, Colonel Tihomir Blaskic, in his order, appoints Mr. Mario Cerkez as a coordinator to prepare the ground, so to speak, for the formation of the Vitez Brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. And now the next document, third document, at least the number, 23rd of March, 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: One of those documents, if not all of them, have already been, I guess, presented by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Yes. Some of them, yes. I cannot claim in this moment, but I guess that one which is just numbered 81/2 was entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, could you explain this to me? In your defence case, what importance do you attach to the presentation of these documents to the witness for the witness just to state what is in those documents? If we look at the previous document which is submitted, I think it needs no commentary, and the witness just says that indeed the document states that Cerkez is the Commander of the brigade and, as is stated in this other one, that he is in charge of organising, supervising, coordinating, administrative activities, et cetera. I don't think this is necessary, because this has been submitted already. The document exists. That we know. So I think you should take into account what has been said to you so far and present a case in a relevant way, and that is to say, as to the elements that have to be taken into account, in order to present your case. I think you've got to focus on this. It is really superfluous to come back to facts that we are aware of just for a witness to tell you, "Yes, I'm reading paragraph 2 of this order." This is really not relevant for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be mindful of your caution. We wanted to adduce all the documents which are of relevance for the establishment of the brigade, because yesterday the question was raised again as to the date of the establishment of the brigade. I think that is a relevant question. Because we have to really establish whether in those days, on the eve of the conflict, my client had already a brigade or not, and when did he have that brigade. I think we should simply clarify once and for all the sequence of events, who established it, when was it established, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But the problem, Mr. Kovacic, is this: That we're going to get into a very considerable muddle if you're going to produce documents which have already been produced and already have numbers. And I'm not going to stop you now, because you've already organised it, but in future, I must ask you, if you're going to produce documents, that we go by the original number and we don't introduce another set with a different number. It will lead to chaos if this sort of thing goes on. Now, the last one that we had, I suspect at least two of these we've already seen, and in future can you concentrate and simply refer to the original number as presented by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Certainly, Your Honour. There is no doubt. The idea was only to put here in one place all four available and relevant documents related to that issue, and particularly because yesterday there was the issue raised of reality of that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: What is the issue? Mr. Nice, can you help? What's the issue?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The actual documents, which -- the documents, many of which we've put in, indeed speak for themselves. The issue is the de facto state of power of Mr. Cerkez before the actual formation, or the de jure formation of the brigade in March of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That's a matter of evidence, but you're not arguing with the documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I'm not arguing with the documents, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: And surely, Your Honour, I will not introduce the documents which are already registered, but I have to mention that there are indeed quite a lot of documents which were introduced a couple of times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: But if it's happened in the past, it should stop. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I will stop it. That is the only occasion when I felt that it should be practical to have them all connected together once, for the purpose of practicality. But I will not do that again.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Sajevic, the third document of the 23rd of March, that is, the list -- you already had time to go through it -- this is a list of people -- will you please explain what does it mean? What is the significance of this?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is simply, the President of the HVO is requested to approve the composition of the brigade that we could come up with at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that this is a document which the HVO government, that is, the civilian authorities, sends to the Operative Zone, that is, Blaskic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it is the civilian government is telling Blaskic, the army, "We agree with this. This is our proposal"?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is the Territorial Defence concept that we talked about. It is the municipality which organises its local defence?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the municipal brigade will then come, according to the chain of command, under the Operative Zone?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what about its funding?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the municipality, by and large.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the last document, which, as Their Honours have already mentioned, has already been adduced, the document of the 24th of March, 1993 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't know. Shall we give it a number or shall we just put the number that it's already been given?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The last occasion we will use a new number, but in the future they are to have the original number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The document of the 23rd of March, 1993 will be numbered D82/2; and the last document, D83/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This document I do not think requires any comment. Do you agree that it corresponds with the facts about what you know?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that you, members of the Command, on that particular day, the day when Cerkez was formally appointed the Commander, also came to consider this day as the day of the formation of the brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that as of that moment you became intensively involved in the organisation of the Brigade Command?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was your priority? What was your objective that you laid before yourselves?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Our objective was to form, to establish the Command of the brigade, to see in formation terms what units should this brigade have, to try to make some skeletons of those units so as to enable it to function, to organise the command post, and that was done in those days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in those days did you continue sending shifts to Vlasic?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, shifts were not sent to Vlasic but to Zlatka Vode. But yes, there was no interruption. Shifts continued to go out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I used the wrong term. Slatka Vode Kamenjas; is that it?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is it correct that soldier Bertovic was performing this job alone and more or less routinely?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And at that time, until the end of March, did you ever think, regardless of all sorts of events, but did it ever occur to you that there might be a direct confrontation, that is, an all-out war between the BH army and the HVO? At that time, if you could give us your view.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. At that time it never crossed my mind that something like that might happen, not even in the worst of nightmares.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Until the 16th of April 1993, when the conflict began, or perhaps the day before that, could you give us a rough estimate, in a couple of sentences, regarding the level of organisation or the degree to which the brigade had been organised by the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me see. By the 15th or 16th of April, it was a very short period of time, and it is well-nigh impossible to organise a brigade as a brigade in line with its formation concept as to how it should look like. I do not think that even much stronger, much richer countries could do it in such a short period of time. Because the formation of the Vitez Brigade, we called it a brigade, but all the military experts the world over know how strong a brigade needs to be. And I can freely say that we never had a brigade. We still do not have it, all these years after the end of the war. I'm a hundred per cent sure that to this day we have not yet organised a proper brigade in formation times. So we were simply involved in an attempt to organise certain groups in some parts of the municipality and to somehow bring them together, to try to make them into wholes. We cannot speak about formation entities and units, because those were nonexistent, but simply in order to coordinate their work easier, to send them out, and that was what we were involved in.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Perhaps we may come back to it for further clarification, but I should simply like to show you a document and ask you to explain the document for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would the usher please help me.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document D84/2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, this is a very, very poor printed copy from a different case, and I have a handwritten copy of the same document in Croatian. Will you please look at the date and the time and the contents.

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is just another proof corroborating what I said before. It was only as late as the 14th of April that the request was sent out for the replenishment of the Vitez Brigade to the Defence Office.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what, according to you, does this document means?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that the first men began to be enlisted in the brigade, which should number, I don't know, 1.000 something. So we were merely asking the Defence Office to officially send us men for their wartime assignment in the brigade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does this mean that it is correct to say that the Defence Office, in line with the concept that we spoke about, was to choose men based on their profile, on their specialisation, which you would then assign to the brigade? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that at that time you had a certain number of men, those going through those shifts, and that they were the only force that you had at the time?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, and that is why here we have a very short deadline, the 20th of April, to comply with this task. But of course that deadline could not be complied with. And the next one -- but then we had a couple of those groups of volunteers on whom we could rely for the organisation of shifts, and Mario, therefore, thought that perhaps they should be given a shorter deadline, or rather a very short deadline, to comply with this task, to expedite the whole business.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And would you agree that at that time that you mentioned, those groups from the lists which were activated, that they were -- that they did not exceed 300?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, not more than that. Not more than that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you agree --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I don't know whether that's in dispute, but you led that evidence. You do understand, Mr. Kovacic, that if you lead evidence: "Do you agree, from the list you were activated, that they did not exceed 300?" Now, I take it that that is an issue which is central to this case, and by giving the evidence yourself, you destroy its value. You must ask questions of this sort in a neutral way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. I certainly will, but I thought that 300 is indisputable. It is entered by the Prosecution, and we, at that time, did not contest it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, just ask the witness and let him -- he was there. Let him give his evidence about what the position was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BENNOUNA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kovacic, you have to be logical. Either this figure is not challenged, then there's no use having the witness talk about it; or there is a need for his testimony, then you must put a neutral question to him. You can't say, "I'm going to lead on this because it is not challenged," because that is equivalent to a waste of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: My apologies. I will try to avoid such situations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you tell us, please: In the evening of the 15th of April, 1993, where were you?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at home in my apartment. I was ill.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And did you -- were you summoned to the Command then?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Will you tell us, in your own words, who happened to be there and what were you told then?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was bedridden, and around 1900 in the evening, the officer on duty in the brigade, I think it was Josip Zuljevic, who called me on the telephone and said that the Commander had ordered me to come to the brigade, to the offices. And I said that I was really ill, that I was running a high fever, of 40 degrees C, and he said, "Right. Very well," and put down the receiver. And then later on, a couple of hours later, he called again and said that I should come to the Command premises at whatever cost.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic, yes. Would that be a convenient moment? We'll adjourn now for half an hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one matter I'm going to raise before we go on. Mr. Nice, I wonder if you could give us your assistance on this matter which considers this practice of putting in duplicate exhibits. Now, it may be that it's been going on for sometime and somehow we haven't really focussed on it, but it's going to lead to complete chaos in final submissions and in the judgement if there are duplicate exhibits. So I think over the recess, we will need your assistance in the matter so that when we come back, we will find out where the duplicates are and all duplicates will simply be removed, and we'll simply have one exhibit. I mean the rules should be this, that once the document or anything else is exhibited, that is the mark which it has in the trial. I suspect what has been happening, and I'm afraid it's -- we've only really focussed on it with Mr. Kovacic, is that the documents are being put in perhaps because it was thought more convenient that they were all together, but nonetheless, it's a -- the knock on effect is to create a confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. We'll, of course, do all we can to help. I think the position is that -- I don't think we've put in any duplicates. I hope not. I'm sure not in, in fact. You will find when you come to consider the outstanding exhibits submitted by the Kordic Defence that there are very large numbers of duplicates there. Now, you've had a filing - not a filing, I can't remember what we've put in, either a filing or a document in tabulated form - to assist you in making your decision about the Kordic outstanding exhibits and we have identified there, I think, the exhibits that are duplicated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, I think probably what we shall do is order those to be removed. If they are already exhibited, it's pointless to have them in another time line. It may be convenient for documents, for lists to be produced where documents -- where parties want to refer to documents in a particular order but, nonetheless, they should then, nonetheless, be within the old exhibit system. Once a document is exhibited, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Two very short points. In fact, I think that where they have duplicated documents, the Kordic Defence have also put it on their indices so it's quite easy to pick up. The second point which we shouldn't overlook is this: Where a transcript reference is to the other exhibit, the second produced exhibit, somehow we've got to be able to capture that that relates to the first exhibit. That isn't going to be that easy but maybe wherever -- if we forget, for the time being, the documents recently submitted by the Kordic Defence and we freeze the position now, then what we will be looking for is within the volumes of materials provided by the Defence, the two "D" series of exhibits. We should perhaps prepare a little schedule that says D, XYZ/1 equals Z whatever it is. Then for us looking at LiveNote and preparing either closing submissions or judgement, if we aren't sure what a document is, it will be easy for us to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, it's as well that we are on to it now because it really is a recipe for total confusion. The exhibits should be referred to by their original exhibit number so that will mean their Z number. If there are collections in that -- in the Defence exhibits, either we shall rule about, because they are duplicates, or if there is argument which persuades us otherwise, they will simply be in the bundle but under their original exhibit nomenclature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Ms. Verhaag has apparently been carefully tracking these, and she may already have, I think, a schedule similar that will enable her in the negotiations that you've instructed us to have with Registry over outstanding Defence exhibits to prepare a document that will guide us all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It will be much easier. There is so much paper in this case, it will be much easier. And I'm minded at the moment to say that there is no duplicates in any form, and we'll simply return them. Yes, Mr. Kovacic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would not like to go into a debate, but perhaps I should present our position in a word or two. There is no doubt that until now, the practice in this case was that on many occasions, and I can't even give the exact numbers, that the same documents were introduced under different numbers. That is a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: If it has been, it's regrettable. It's obviously a matter which the Trial Chamber didn't focus on, but it's a regrettable practice which should stop and a document should simply have one number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fully agree with Your Honour. I do apologise that I was the person who duplicated things today, but the point was to link-up four documents here, because the indictment does say that the brigade was established in 1992. So my only objective was to link them up. I do apologise if I caused this problem now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: There's no need to apologise, but it's quite simply done. You produce your four documents but with their original numbers so it would be Z this, Z the next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There is absolutely no loss to you by that device. You can still make use of the Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Kovacic, if you would follow that practice in future, it might be helpful. If tomorrow you would give us the numbers of the Z numbers of the documents which have been introduced today, if you could simply do it in tabulated form with the Prosecution, perhaps, so we can alter our records. But no need to do it today. Yes, let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Sajevic, you remember where we stopped. You said that you were taken out of bed and that you received a phone call. Did you go to headquarters then?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went between 2000 hours and 2030, something like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who did you find there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In headquarters, I found a few of my colleagues which was almost normal, because there was somebody always who was in the field here and there, and I found Mr. Cerkez there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So Cerkez was already there when you arrived; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Cerkez tell you, the officers who were present there?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I asked him why he was calling me and what was up. I had no idea what was going on and what was so urgent, why did I have to come in that ill. He explained to me that there were several incidents in the recent past with the BH army and that there were some indications that there might be a more serious incident, something to that effect. And that we should get a group of people together in order to secure the road, communication towards Kruscica and Vranjska. Perhaps at a given point in time, we should stop the BH army forces from entering town.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Who is "we" in this context? Who is "we" referring to?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm referring to those men who were in that period of the establishment brigade who were with us, I mean, who were on the lists. That's what I mean. I mean the HVO soldiers and the members of the Viteska Brigade who were members at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sajevic, did Cerkez say anything about the sources of this information, how did he get this information or this estimate?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, I asked him whether there was an order in writing for such activity, and he said that there wasn't any. He said that he received this information at the Command.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The Commander of the Operative Zone at that time was who?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Commander was Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Cerkez say anything about that, that he would get a written order, or did you ask about it at all, or was this only natural to expect one?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I asked, and he said that during the night a written order should arrive but that it should not say anything new. That is a situation that was being repeated for the umpteenth time. Our attention was being drawn to the fact that we should be a bit more cautious. This time perhaps it could be more serious, because there had been mounting tensions between the BH army and the HVO, as I already mentioned, after the provocations and incidents that had already occurred, on a smaller scale, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Major Sajevic, did this information lead to the conclusion that an attack was expected for sure, or was there a degree of assessment involved, estimation?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not get the impression that there was 100 per cent certitude involved as far as this attack is involved. This was an assumption that there could be such an attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. When did Cerkez leave the Command?

utterances.speaker: ZELJKO SAJEVIC [Resumed]
